findings.where: Screen 1 text and read (definition of a differential equation)
findings.what: "A rule that ties a rate to the thing itself is a differential equation" leaves out screen 11's dy/dt = 2t, which ties the rate to time only, so make it "to the thing itself, or to time" (the explain text already says "and sometimes to time").

findings.where: Screens 1 to 13 (no screen carries the model's limits)
findings.what: A steps lesson shows only the frame, so the explain text's "Newton's rule is a simplified model" and the ignores note never reach Dan; add one short sentence, on screen 1 or 7, naming it Newton's law of cooling and saying it is a simple model that holds best for a modest gap.
"losing a tenth of its gap to the room per minute" can be read as a fixed drop each whole minute, the very slip screen 2 tests, so say "its rate, in °C a minute, is a tenth of its gap" instead.

No screen starts from what Dan knows: the brief's bridge from i = C dv/dt is missing, and so is the link to the cooling curve from Exponentials lesson 3; one short sentence on screen 1 or 5 would anchor it.
The term "first order" from the brief never appears on a screen, so lesson 5's "second order" will have nothing to contrast with; one sentence on screen 1 or 3 would fix that.

"So the rule fixes the shape" is loose, because the 10 °C curve rises and the 20 °C line is flat; "the rule fixes the slopes" matches the finish line, "The rule gives the slope. The start picks the curve."
The line is drawn red from 0.6 s, including at 80 °C, where the label says it matches, before the 50 °C and 20 °C marks give the reason; grow it in ink and turn it red once the 50 °C mark shows.
